data.one_liner: FaaS framework for writing portable Dart functions.
data.what_it_does: An open source FaaS (Function as a Service) framework that lets you write lightweight functions in Dart which run portably across local machines, Google Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Knative-based environments without writing explicit HTTP server boilerplate.
use_when: You want to deploy serverless Dart functions to Google Cloud Run or Knative environments.
You want to handle HTTP requests or CloudEvents without writing custom server request-handling logic.
avoid_when: You need an officially supported Google Cloud Functions Dart runtime (currently not provided).
You require an official enterprise-level SLA or deprecation policy, as this is a community-supported project.
strengths: Portable between multiple serverless and container platforms like Cloud Run and App Engine.
Supports automatic unmarshaling of CloudEvents and handling of JSON data.
Removes the boilerplate of setting up an HTTP server and request-handling logic.
weaknesses: Community-supported project with no official level of support or SLA.
Google Cloud Functions does not currently provide an officially supported Dart language runtime.
data.setup_notes: Annotate functions with @CloudFunction() and run inside serverless containers or local environments.
